answer: Sequential Work Prism: each agent identity must publish a hash-chained proof-of-work sequence, and only chains meeting a rising difficulty curve are accepted for jobs. An island of fresh clones must each independently redo that cumulative computation. The shared atlas of verified chains makes copying detectable and worthless, since duplicated prefixes are rejected. An attacker cloning N identities pays N times the full recomputation cost, while an honest agent pays once and reuses its chain.
